overview: Assessment of the city's stationary energy sector covering electricity and fuel consumption (LPG, PNG) across residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal buildings, plus Solar PV adoption levels.
current_situation: 51.6 million sq.m. of city-wide buildings (70% residential); ~145,000 sq.m. of municipal buildings (37% residential, 36% non-residential). 83% of building energy use is grid electricity. Residential consumers = 88% of connections, 48% of consumption; industrial 33%; commercial 13%. Municipal building electricity consumption = 44,72,053 kWh (Apr 2024-Mar 2025, ESR). PCMC solar PV installed capacity = 2,808 kW (since 2018) generating 6.07 million units/year; proposed additional 57 MW.

baseline_data.metric: Buildings & Energy share of city GHG emissions
PCMC installed rooftop solar capacity (cumulative since 2018)

challenges: Insufficient data on coal/fossil-fuel use in industries, commercial and residential areas
Slow grid decarbonisation - PCMC lacks large-scale municipal solar procurement, community solar, or microgrids
Slower renewable-energy adoption at major junctions (traffic signals not fully solar-powered)
Weak ECBC (Energy Conservation Building Code) compliance
Low adoption of passive design (shading, ventilation, cool roofs)
Informal housing constraints - 7% of households (Census 2011, base 427,356 HHs) live under temporary roofing, limiting solar access
Institutional capacity limits for technical expertise, staffing, inter-departmental coordination
climate_risks: Rising urban heat increases cooling-energy demand (cross-referenced from Urban Heat Risk chapter, Doc A p.80-92)
existing_initiatives: 100% LED lighting across all PCMC buildings and streetlights
Solar power systems installed at PCMC main office and all 8 regional (A-H) zone offices - 11,614 kWh generation
Waste-to-Energy plant at Moshi - 14 MW electricity generation from waste processing
50 TPD bio-methanation plant at Moshi (hotel/restaurant/canteen waste to biogas/bio-CNG)
Plastic-to-fuel plant (5 TPD, since 2010, BVG Pvt. Ltd. PPP) - 65,147 litres furnace oil produced in 2024-25
22 EV charging stations planned at key locations (PCMC HQ, Nigdi, Bhosari, Chikhali, Pimple Saudagar, metro stations)
Green Society Initiative - rates/rewards housing societies on waste segregation, composting, solar, rainwater harvesting, wastewater recycling
GRIHA and SVAGRIHA green-building rating incentive programs (premium discounts, property-tax rebates)

strategies.name: Building a citywide renewable-energy ecosystem by expanding solar PV capacity, enabling greater private-sector adoption and enhancing incentives and support mechanisms.
Accelerate the transition to low-carbon buildings through ECBC compliance, mandatory energy-efficient design, and wider adoption of green building certifications.
Enable industrial clusters to transition to low-carbon operations through energy efficiency, cleaner fuels, electrification, process upgrades, and increased green-power uptake.
Accelerate the shift to PNG, electric, and other clean-fuel systems across residential and commercial users by 2040.
Build institutional and community capacity through awareness programmes, sensitisation workshops, and technical training.
